design_intent: Tree-centered visual argument replacing a box-based process overview; generated candidates are reviewed before adoption.
base:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Primary request: create the main method figure for EvoTrace in a top-tier ML conference paper. The previous figure failed because it was a row of equal-sized process boxes; this must be a conceptual, idea-led scientific illustration. A large evolving ALGORITHM LINEAGE TREE is the visual protagonist. The figure must make the combination of a population's selection and a tree's developmental experience visually understandable. Treat composition like a scientific argument with a clear focal point, supporting evidence and a return of experience into future design.
Style: elegant editorial vector-like academic illustration on pure white; thin precise strokes, sharp large sans-serif typography, flat restrained color, very generous negative space, subtle translucent tree-region highlights. Dark ink #253341, teal #217C7E retained algorithms, blue #3E67AA newly generated algorithms / design action, amber #D99530 experiences, cool gray #B3BDC3 removed details. Understated small section labels. High-resolution wide landscape master figure, requested around 3072 by 1800 pixels if possible; prioritize legible scientific drawing over small dense text.
Avoid: thick colored title bars, glossy/gradient balls, dashboard cards, equal boxes in a rigid grid, generic flowchart chains, robot/brain icons, database/external memory-bank icons, checkmarks or promotional slogans, long paragraphs, empirical scores or fictional performance data, task-specific benchmark names, implementation plumbing, parameter tables.
Mechanism invariants:
- A candidate algorithm is a node; a main-parent edge is a developmental relation. Retained internal nodes as well as leaves remain usable development starting points.
- The tree genuinely grows by adding a NEW evaluated child under a retained parent P that may already have children. A crossover reference R on another branch is only an auxiliary input into design; do not give the new child two main-parent edges.
- Selection removes explicit program detail while reflective simplification writes path experience ON a reconnected EDGE and pruned-branch experience ON the nearest retained NODE. Experience is located in the tree, not in an external box or memory bank.
- Exact local region: A -> B -> C -> D and B -> X, with only A,D retained. B,C and old S_B feed edge note V_AD on A->D. X and old S_A feed node note S_A on A. X has original parent B. Each removed node has one destination.
- A single LLM design event reads current code and task-relevant tree experience. Refine reads formation/local trials; Crossover reads diverging branches; Explore reads direction ideas and experience. These are ALTERNATIVE choices in a single search, not three simultaneous agents. Do not show experience directly changing the parent-sampling formula.
- The next evaluated program is attached back to the SAME tree, visibly continuing evolution. Reflection and generation are distinct operations.
- Show the framework shared by V1/V2; omit their numerical thresholds from this main figure.
Words in the image must be short and spelled correctly. Only a few labels; geometry must carry most of the explanation. S = branch experience, V = path experience.

Composition: one asymmetric, richly structured lineage tree sweeping from a small virtual root at the LEFT toward a branching growth frontier at upper RIGHT, occupying about 60% of the canvas. Draw around 18-24 meaningful algorithm nodes in several related directions, with a strong main development path, side trials and one cross-branch reference. Include both solid retained branches and faint gray ghost details near a region being simplified. Use region halos and tiny note glyphs attached to actual edges/nodes, not a big container.
Visually express THREE interconnected levels with unequal emphasis:
1. The big tree itself labelled "Tree-structured population", dominant, with a small label "Select useful algorithms" beside a few retained high-emphasis nodes. At the upper-right frontier show a BLUE new child labelled "new algorithm" joining teal parent P; P is explicitly an INTERNAL node with existing children. Label that local action "Continued development".
2. A large but subordinate irregular zoom callout in the LOWER LEFT, tethered to an older region of the tree. Title "Reflective simplification". Inside show the exact A-B-C-D / B-X region lightly drawn BEFORE and its A->D counterpart AFTER, with the path collapsing into amber V_AD on the edge and the side branch collapsing into amber S_A on the node. It should feel like a magnified local transformation of the actual population, not a separate generic pipeline. The short captions are "contract paths" and "prune branches". Make old S_B -> V_AD and X -> S_A clear with two small amber evidence trails.
3. At LOWER RIGHT, an open, compact design vignette titled "Design from the tree". It contains one modest LLM/code glyph with the label "Generate & evaluate" (not a robot), a small current-code sheet labelled P, and a secondary reference sheet R with a thin dashed blue connector from a DIFFERENT tree branch. Three small unboxed textual choices around the vignette: "Refine", "Crossover", "Explore", each tied to a tiny path, bifurcation or direction-view glyph. They feed ONE design event. A thin amber curve takes located experience from the main tree into this design event; a broad but unobtrusive blue return curve goes from this event to the newly added upper-right child, closing the search loop.
Emphasize a visually compelling handoff: old program details fade to gray while warm amber notes remain on the surviving tree; those notes inform a new blue branch. Fine irregular tree geometry, editorial white space and carefully weighted annotations, not forced symmetry. Keep the central tree connected and the simplified inset scientifically exact. No giant title across the page; just the method name "EvoTrace" modestly at upper left and the few mechanism labels.

Composition: a continuous evolving genealogy across a wide white canvas, like a scientific lineage illustration with three subtly overlapping temporal states, NOT three equal panels. The visual center is a dominant simplified TREE WITH EXPERIENCE, larger than the older ghost tree to its left and the new growth to its right. Leftmost older details are light gray; a few retained anchors and vigorous lineages stay dark teal. Small faded intermediate nodes visually fold into amber edge notes, and extinct side branches fold into amber node notes. The central tree remains structurally related to the historical tree so viewers see what survived, what was compressed and where memory stayed.
Top-level reading direction is left to right: "Develop" (small), "Select and distill" (dominant center), "Develop with experience" (upper right). Do not use rectangular stage containers or big arrows between boxes. Let actual retained paths, dotted ghost links and short amber transfer curves express the transformation.
Below the dominant center, one small connected magnification shows the exact A->B->C->D plus B->X region becoming A->D with V_AD on the edge and S_A on A. Preserve the given old-experience ownership; do not bury it in dense labels.
On the far right show an explicitly internal retained node P with existing descendants and one extra new blue child. Just beneath that frontier, a compact "Tree-conditioned design" vignette reads a highlighted ancestor path, a second branch R and a broad direction-view arc from the central population. The tiny text "Refine / Crossover / Explore" denotes one chosen operator, feeding ONE LLM/code event; an amber experience line enters this event, and its evaluated output becomes that one new child under P.
This alternative is an expansive, graceful lineage illustration: thin ink edges, subtle translucent colored route highlights, orange experience slips physically attached to edges and nodes, a blue future addition. Core visual message: selection focuses the population while located developmental experience survives simplification and informs new growth. Sparse labels, no performance metrics, no interface-card styling.
